justifications.reason: This is the vendored lodepng implementation used by the inherited QuakeSpasm compatibility codebase. It remains a single translation unit because splitting a third-party codec source would increase merge and verification risk without advancing QGE domain ownership.
justifications.mitigation: Do not land new QGE behavior in this file. Treat changes as vendor-sync or security/codec fixes only; if image codec ownership becomes a QGE requirement, wrap it behind a focused QGE image-codec module boundary instead of editing the vendor implementation.

justifications.reason: This is the paired lodepng public header from the vendored codec compatibility source. Its size reflects upstream API and documentation, not a QGE subsystem boundary.
justifications.mitigation: Keep QGE code isolated from this header through existing QuakeSpasm call sites. Any future QGE image IO surface should use a narrow adapter module boundary and leave the vendored header intact except for vendor-sync updates.

justifications.reason: This is the vendored miniz compression implementation carried by the QuakeSpasm compatibility tree. It is oversized by design as a self-contained third-party library, not because QGE gameplay or Moonlab authority is concentrated there.
justifications.mitigation: Avoid QGE feature work in this file. Compression changes should be vendor-sync, bugfix, or security-only; if QGE needs owned compression evidence, add a separate adapter/test surface instead of splitting this vendor file.

justifications.reason: This inherited QuakeSpasm file owns BSP/model loading, texture metadata, and lightmap setup used as the classic reference asset compatibility boundary. Splitting it before QGE fully owns model import would risk changing reference semantics that current publication captures rely on.
justifications.mitigation: Keep QGE changes at explicit hook or adapter boundaries and validate with vanilla/QGE capture matrices. The migration path is focused QGE-owned model, texture, and lightmap import modules once those artifacts no longer depend on classic loader internals.

justifications.reason: This inherited common-runtime file contains broad QuakeSpasm compatibility utilities, command-line handling, and filesystem glue that remain part of the host/reference runtime rather than the QGE authority surface.
justifications.mitigation: Do not add new QGE domain logic here. Route QGE behavior through focused qge/ modules or explicit hook files, and only touch common.c for host compatibility fixes with regression coverage.

justifications.reason: This is inherited QuakeSpasm menu/UI compatibility code. It is large because it preserves the classic menu system, while current QGE/Moonlab work uses it only as host UI and not as an authority subsystem.
justifications.mitigation: Keep QGE runtime ownership and publication evidence out of this file. If QGE needs owned UI telemetry, add a focused QGE UI/overlay module and leave classic menu behavior as reference compatibility.

justifications.reason: This inherited SDL/OpenGL video backend remains the platform windowing and display compatibility layer. Its monolithic shape reflects upstream video bootstrap constraints, not hidden QGE renderer authority.
justifications.mitigation: Keep QGE rendering authority in qge/ and qge_hooks.c, and use stream/harness tests to validate any display bootstrap change. The future migration path is a narrow QGE display module boundary once renderer ownership no longer needs the classic video path.

justifications.reason: This inherited host-command compatibility surface preserves classic console, save/demo, and server command behavior. It remains large because those commands are tightly coupled to Quake host state used as the reference runtime.
justifications.mitigation: Avoid placing QGE authority in host commands. Add QGE commands through narrow, tested hooks and migrate stable QGE command handling into focused modules when the ownership boundary is no longer coupled to classic host state.

justifications.reason: This file is the current compatibility boundary between the upstream QuakeSpasm runtime and QGE-owned rendering, visibility, Noesis, physics, audio, and telemetry hooks. Keeping the hooks co-located avoids splitting hot frame-state code before the engine ownership seams are stable.
justifications.mitigation: New work should keep changes narrowly scoped, covered by tests and stream evidence, and move stable subsystems into focused modules when the QGE ownership boundary no longer needs direct access to Quake renderer and server internals. The active renderer extraction candidates are world texture/lightmap sampling, alias-model skin sampling, alias-normal lighting, tone/display conversion, and stream evidence emission; graphics fixes that touch qge_hooks.c should update the state docs with live capture evidence until those helpers are split. The 2026-05-21 alias-skin viewmodel, one-texel bilinear world-texture, world-surface blue-balance, world texture-detail restore, 2026-05-22 luma-floor/detail-restore, and 2026-05-22 viewmodel-lighting/alias-normal/edge-cadence slices are intentionally still in qge_hooks.c because the projected-triangle sampler, surface texture/lightmap contexts, spatial RGB/depth buffers, palette LUT, model-cache aliases, and stream ownership counters are static to this boundary. The 2026-05-22 164822 edge-cadence follow-up remains a constant-only first-person brightness and edge-density adjustment with fixed-view capture evidence and no named world-crop movement. The 2026-05-22 e1m2 micro-surface projection slice is limited to routing sub-pixel projected BSP surfaces through the existing owned projected-polygon/micro-fill encoder; live evidence is diagnostics/quake_graphics/20260522-231423 and the stricter two-map breadth pack diagnostics/breadth_evidence/20260522-231644. The 2026-05-22 backend-gate prefix change is a one-line telemetry normalization so tools/qge_perf_summary.py can ingest the live QGE render-bridge probe consistently; refreshed evidence is diagnostics/breadth_evidence/20260522-235635 with backend_gate_render_bridge_run_count=7. The 2026-05-23 e1m8 entity-cull ownership fix is kept here because projected entity bounds, frame snapshots, ownership counters, and render stream telemetry are all static in this hook boundary; live evidence is diagnostics/quake_graphics/20260523-150006 and the eight-map breadth pack diagnostics/breadth_evidence/20260523-150050. The migration target is a focused QGE renderer module once those dependencies are lifted out of the hook file.

justifications.reason: This reducer is still the single compatibility point for stream manifest parsing, Noesis action traces, gameplay outcome telemetry, quality gates, scoring, and ICC evidence emission while the Noesis evidence schema is changing quickly.
justifications.mitigation: Keep additions schema-focused and unit-tested. Once the no-script gameplay telemetry stabilizes, split gameplay parsing, scoring, and ICC evidence emission into focused helper modules.

justifications.reason: This tool is a temporary compatibility facade and single reproducibility orchestrator for the current publication bundle. It copies source artifacts, builds resource ledgers, selects Moonlab simulator/native replay jobs, emits hardware handoff contracts, and writes the ICC manifest so the pack can be regenerated from one CLI while the publishable-results schema is still moving.
justifications.mitigation: Keep domain logic in focused tools such as qge_asset_inventory.py, qge_asset_requirements.py, qge_registered_asset_intake.py, qge_moonlab_job_runner.py, qge_moonlab_qae_transpile.py, qge_moonlab_submission_bundle.py, qge_moonlab_full_game_plan.py, and qge_moonlab_deployment_gate.py. Limit qge_publication_pack.py to orchestration and manifest assembly; the 2026-05-23 registered-asset intake slice adds only a reproduce-command pointer here while keeping candidate scanning, BSP validation, copy planning, and ICC evidence in tools/qge_registered_asset_intake.py. The 2026-05-24 Moonlab submission-readiness slices keep QAE readout payload generation in tools/qge_moonlab_qae_transpile.py and circuit payload classification, control-plane readiness status, Markdown, and ICC evidence in tools/qge_moonlab_submission_bundle.py; qge_publication_pack.py only writes those focused tools' JSON/Markdown/ICC artifacts into the pack manifest. When the publication schema stabilizes, split artifact packing, resource-ledger assembly, Moonlab job assembly, and ICC evidence emission into separate modules with the existing contract tests as migration coverage.
